items.followUp: State two properties of a liquid suitable for use in a thermometer.

rubric.why: A thermometer is defined by its use in measuring temperature.
rubric.how: State that it is an instrument used to measure temperature.

rubric.why: Uniform expansion allows the liquid's change in length to indicate temperature changes reliably.
rubric.description: Gives uniform expansion as a property.
rubric.how: State that the liquid expands uniformly as its temperature changes.

rubric.why: A suitable temperature range allows the thermometer to measure a wider range of temperatures.
rubric.how: State that the liquid has a high boiling point or a low freezing point.

rubric.why: These properties make the liquid easier to see or make it more responsive to temperature changes.
rubric.how: State that the liquid is visible, does not wet the glass, or has a high coefficient of expansion.

modelAnswer: A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature.
The liquid used in a thermometer should expand uniformly with temperature.
It should have a high boiling point and a low freezing point.
It should be visible and should not wet the glass.

items.followUp: A force of 30 N acts on a square surface of side 20 mm. Calculate the pressure on the surface.

rubric.why: The force and the side length converted to SI units are needed for the calculation.
rubric.description: Records the given force and converts the side length to metres.
rubric.how: Write F = 20 N and convert 10 mm to 0.01 m.

rubric.why: Pressure requires the area of the square surface, found by squaring its side.
rubric.description: Calculates the area of the square.
rubric.how: Use A = side² to find A = 1 × 10⁻⁴ m².

rubric.why: This is the correct relationship between pressure, force, and area.
This is the correct pressure obtained using the given force and square area, with the required unit.
rubric.description: Substitutes and calculates the pressure with its unit.
rubric.how: Substitute into P = F/A and give the result as 2 × 10⁵ Pa.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 20 N, side = 10 mm = 0.01 m.

items.followUp: Define a derived unit and give two examples.

rubric.why: Derived units are obtained by combining base units.
rubric.how: State that derived units are formed by combining base units.

rubric.why: The question asks for two examples, and each listed pair contains two derived SI units.
rubric.description: Gives names of two derived units.
rubric.how: Name any two valid derived units, such as the newton and joule.

modelAnswer: Derived units are the units formed by combining base units through multiplication or division.
Two examples are the newton (N) and the joule (J).
